A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JETTS benchmark. All 36 pages of each version, including Appendices A–C, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables that support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original evaluations of judge models for response reranking, beam search, and critique-based refinement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the benchmark results in Tables 3–15 and qualitative critique case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same pairwise and single-rating reranking procedures, beam search with and without lookahead, and iterative critique-based refinement. The prose revisions do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Table 1 retains the same eight datasets across math reasoning, code generation, and instruction following. The evaluated scenarios are unchanged, including the restriction of beam search to math and code.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same judge models, prompted Llama-3.1-8B baseline, three outcome reward models, Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, and greedy, random, oracle, and majority-vote comparators.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, metrics, prompts, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Both use one greedy plus nine sampled responses for reranking, temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95 for sampling, (10, 2) beam search with depth limit 10, and (1, 9) refinement.

E4.justification: v2 removes the secondary analysis relating normalized helpfulness to greedy performance as a proxy for task difficulty, presented in v1 Section 4.3 and Figure 11. The lookahead, domain-specific prompting, rating-leniency, and critique case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same two-sided one-sample t-tests and significance thresholds, and retained analyses use unchanged statistical reporting. Removing the difficulty-regression results does not change the estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: The removed v1 Figure 11 reported helpfulness-versus-greedy-performance regression coefficients of -0.08 for math, -0.16 for code, and -0.87 for instruction following, with significance annotations. These results disappear; the leaderboard and numerical results in Tables 3–15 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Normalized helpfulness in Equation 1, refinement ratios in Equations 2–3, and the diagnostic metric definitions in Section 4.4 are unchanged. Condensed explanations and relocation of the metric diagram introduce no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces v1's assertion that each task covers all three domains with benchmark-wide three-domain coverage. This narrows the description to fit the unchanged math/code-only beam search. The abstract, novelty claim, and headline conclusions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 drops the interpretation that judges become more helpful on harder tasks, especially instruction following, together with the qualification that difficulty depends on generator strength. Other central explanations of judge limitations and refinement failures are retained.

D1.justification: The code link, response-release statement, evaluation implementation notes, vLLM and A100 hardware details, and prompt templates remain unchanged. Appendix figure renumbering and the new reference to existing Table 10 add no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 changes its characterization of finetuned judges from being susceptible to bias to being less susceptible, and removes the domain-specific finetuning qualifier. The bibliography and JETTS's positioning relative to earlier benchmarks otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the introduction, metric explanations, and lookahead discussion, adds an explicit Table 10 reference, and replaces the preprint notice with publication information. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 11 is deleted. The refinement-metric illustration moves from v1 Figure 13 in the main text to an enlarged v2 Figure 26 in Appendix B.3. Other figures are renumbered or repositioned; retained plot contents and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The main methods, comparisons, full benchmark results, and reproducibility material are preserved. v2 improves concision and corrects the introduction's coverage description, while losing one ancillary difficulty analysis and its qualification. The metric illustration remains available in the appendix. These limited changes alter emphasis without materially changing the paper's overall evidential strength.
